about_mission2: Kiwi Lunchbox is built and run by one parent in Flat Bush, Auckland — not a company or a team. I track New Zealand supermarket prices week by week and cost every menu against them, so the numbers you see are the ones I actually record rather than estimates pulled from nowhere.
about_feat1_desc: Generate a complete weekly plan in seconds. Say goodbye to the morning rush and hello to organized, stress-free starts to your day.
about_feat2_desc: Every menu is built from ingredients I have checked are reliably stocked at Woolworths and Pak'nSave. The planner does not sort by season — there is no seasonal data behind it — but the seasonal produce guide covers that separately.
about_feat3_desc: The generator enforces variety across categories so a week is not five sandwiches, and shows an estimated calorie figure per lunch. It is an estimate, not a dietitian's plan, and it does not check a week against Ministry of Health targets.
about_community_desc: Kiwi Lunchbox is constantly improved based on parent feedback from NZ schools. The goal is simple — make healthy eating the easy choice for our kids.

faq_subtitle: Everything you need to know about Kiwi Lunchbox Planner.
faq_still_desc: Can't find the answer you're looking for? Send us a message — we'd love to help.
faq_q1: Is Kiwi Lunchbox Planner free to use?
faq_a1: Yes! The core weekly planner — generating meal plans, viewing recipes, and downloading shopping lists — is completely free. We may introduce premium features in the future, but the essentials will always remain free.
faq_q2: How does the meal plan generator work?
faq_a2: The planner picks 5 lunch menus for the week from the recipe database. It prioritises variety across categories (Sandwich, Hot, Baking, Cold) and applies any allergy or dietary filters you've set. You can also add fridge leftovers or favourite ingredients to influence the selection. It is variety by category — it does not score a week for nutritional balance.
faq_q3: Can I filter for allergies or dietary requirements?
faq_a3: Yes. Before generating your plan you can select Nut Allergy, Dairy Allergy, Gluten Allergy, Egg Allergy, Sesame Allergy, Vegetarian and Vegan, in any combination. The planner excludes matching mains and snacks, and the shopping list is built only from what survives. The two are filtered on different evidence: mains on our own recipe tags; packaged snacks on the allergen declaration printed on the supermarket product we track; fresh fruit and vegetables, and the few snacks whose tracked product carries no declaration, on flags we set by hand. That is how Rice Wheels, a chicken-flavoured rice snack, is kept out of a dairy-free plan: nothing in the name suggests dairy, but the packet declares milk. Sesame is the exception for mains: there is no recipe tag for it, so a main is kept only if none of its ingredients' tracked products declares sesame, and unlabelled bread, pastry and spice ingredients are left out because we cannot check them. If nothing in a snack category qualifies, that slot is left empty rather than filled with something that does not.
faq_a4: We take allergy safety seriously and have carefully tagged every recipe in our database. Snacks are checked against the allergen declaration on the tracked product. We exclude on the declared allergens only — a 'may contain traces of' or 'made on a line that also produces' warning does not remove an item, because almost every packaged snack in a New Zealand supermarket carries one. We also cannot guarantee that the product you buy matches the one we tracked: manufacturers change formulations and cross-contamination can occur. Always read the label on every product you purchase. For severe allergies, consult your healthcare provider.
faq_q5: Where do the supermarket prices come from?
faq_a5: Price estimates are based on the regular shelf prices of specific Woolworths NZ products, refreshed weekly. Prices are approximations and may differ at your local store or on sale days. Pak'nSave and New World prices may vary. Use the estimates as a planning guide rather than exact values.
faq_a6: Calorie estimates are based on standard portion sizes and average nutritional values from generic food databases. They are rough estimates intended to give a ballpark idea of energy content — not a substitute for precise nutritional tracking. Actual calories will vary based on specific brands and portion sizes used.
faq_q7: Can I save or favourite meal plans?
faq_a7: An account is optional — everything on the planner works without one. You can generate a week, download the PDF and print the shopping list as a guest. If you do create an account (email and password; there is no Google or Facebook login), you can star favourite menus so they come up more often, and email a plan to yourself.
faq_q8: Can I download the shopping list?
faq_a8: Yes. Once your weekly plan is generated you can download it as a PDF. For each day it shows the lunch, its main ingredients, the estimated cost and an estimated calorie figure, followed by a shopping list grouped by category (Produce, Meat & Seafood, Dairy & Eggs, Bakery, etc.). The shopping list in the PDF has item names only — per-item prices are shown on the planner screen. With a free account you can also email the PDF to yourself.
faq_q9: Is the app suitable for schools with nut-free policies?
faq_a9: Yes. Enable the 'Nut Allergy' filter and the planner will only suggest nut-free menus, with nut-free snacks alongside them. All menus in our database are reviewed for nut content and packaged snacks are checked against the allergen declaration on the product we track; fresh fruit, vegetables and the few snacks without a declaration are flagged by hand. Cross-contamination warnings are not used to exclude items, so for a school with a strict nut-free policy, still read the packet before it goes in the bag.
faq_q10: What languages does the app support?
faq_a10: Kiwi Lunchbox Planner supports English, Korean (한국어), and Chinese (中文). Use the language selector in the top navigation bar to switch.
faq_q11: Can I suggest new recipes or report an error?
faq_a11: Absolutely! We'd love your feedback. Use our Contact page to send us recipe suggestions, report incorrect allergy tags, or flag any issues. We review all submissions and update the database regularly.
faq_q12: How do I use the fridge leftovers feature?
faq_a12: In the Planner sidebar, you'll find a 'Fridge Leftovers' field. Type in an ingredient you already have (e.g., 'chicken', 'spinach'), and the planner will prioritise menus that use that ingredient. This helps reduce food waste and save money.
faq_q13: Does the app work on mobile?
faq_a13: Yes. Kiwi Lunchbox Planner is fully responsive and works on smartphones and tablets. You can plan your week and view shopping lists on the go.
faq_a14: Supermarket prices are refreshed weekly — every chain column in the price index is read from that chain's own online shop in the same run. New recipes are added in batches rather than on a schedule: the database went from 63 to {menuCount} menus across July 2026 and has been at {menuCount} since. Corrections happen whenever something is found to be wrong — two gluten-free flags were fixed on 20 August 2026, for instance. If you notice a recipe that looks outdated or a price that seems wrong, please tell me via the Contact page.
faq_q15: How do I create my first weekly lunchbox plan?
faq_a15: Getting started is simple and takes under a minute. Visit the Planner page and you'll see a sidebar with customisation options. You can set allergy and dietary filters (nut, dairy, gluten, egg, sesame, vegetarian, vegan), exclude specific ingredients your child doesn't like, and even add fridge leftovers you want to use up. Once you're happy with your settings, click 'Generate Plan' and you'll have a complete 5-day school lunch plan within about 5 seconds. Each day includes a main lunch item with its ingredients, up to two snacks (a fruit or vegetable, plus one from the protein and dairy or savoury crunch group), and an estimated cost from Woolworths NZ prices. You can then download the whole plan as a PDF or, with a free account, email the PDF to yourself. No account is needed for the basic features — just open the page and start planning.
faq_q16: Can I customise the generated plan after it's created?
faq_a16: Yes, one day at a time. Each day card has a 'Swap this day' button that replaces just that day's lunch and its snacks with another recipe that fits the same allergy, excluded-ingredient, prep-style and thermos filters the plan was made with and isn't already in that week; the day's cost, the week total and the shopping list update to match. If no other recipe fits, it says so and leaves the day as it is. To start over, Generate makes a fresh 5-day plan from {menuCount} recipes. Before you generate, you can steer the result: exclude ingredients you'd rather avoid, add something from the fridge in the 'Fridge Leftovers' field so meals using it are favoured, choose prep styles or thermos-friendly meals, and, with a free account, mark lunches you like as favourites so they come up more often.
faq_q17: Does the planner support multiple allergies at the same time?
faq_a17: Yes, absolutely. You can enable as many allergy filters as you need simultaneously. For example, if your child is both nut-free and dairy-free, select both filters and the planner will only suggest meals that are free of both allergens. All seven filters (nut, dairy, gluten, egg, sesame, vegetarian, vegan) can be combined in any combination. The planner will warn you if there are very few recipes available for your specific filter combination, so you'll know if you need to relax one of the restrictions to get a full 5-day plan.
faq_q18: How do you handle cross-contamination warnings?
faq_a18: Our recipes are tagged based on their listed ingredients — if a recipe doesn't contain nuts in its ingredient list, it's tagged as nut-free. However, we cannot account for cross-contamination that may occur during manufacturing of commercial products or in your own kitchen. For children with severe allergies (particularly anaphylaxis risk), we strongly recommend always checking the label of every product you purchase, even if you've bought it before, as manufacturers can change formulations and production lines. Our planner is a planning aid, not a medical device. For severe allergies, please consult your child's allergist or immunologist and inform the school directly.
faq_q19: Can I use the planner for a child with coeliac disease?
faq_a19: As a starting point, yes. The gluten-free filter keeps only the mains we have flagged gluten-free, and snacks whose tracked product declares no gluten (fresh fruit and vegetables are flagged by hand). Recipes with wheat, barley, rye or oats are never flagged gluten-free. Oats are treated as not gluten-free, with no exceptions: under the Australia New Zealand Food Standards Code, a food containing oats cannot be labelled gluten-free. Some gluten-free recipes rely on buying the gluten-free version of a product, such as GF bread, GF pasta or GF crackers, and the ingredient list says so. The flags are our own reading of each recipe, not a certification, and sauces, stocks and other packaged items vary by brand. Coeliac disease requires strict avoidance of even trace amounts of gluten, and cross-contamination in manufacturing is a real concern, so always check that the specific products and brands you buy are gluten-free and suitable for a coeliac diet. Coeliac New Zealand (coeliac.org.nz) maintains a list of certified products that can help with shopping.
faq_q20: How can I reduce my weekly lunchbox budget?
faq_a20: A few things move the number more than the rest. First, protein is what drives a lunchbox budget — the single biggest line in a costed week is usually the meat, so a meat-free day or two saves more than trimming snacks. On our menu set a vegetarian main runs about 40% less than one with meat. Second, check unit price rather than sticker price: a yoghurt pouch can cost two to three times the same yoghurt from a tub even when the pouch is on special. Third, use the planner's 'Fridge Leftovers' field so the week is built around what you already have. Fourth, store choice matters, but less than people assume — across the {basketN} staples I can compare fairly, Pak'nSave came out {basketPct}% cheaper than Woolworths ({basketW} against {basketP}), and about half of that gap sat in just three items: sliced chicken, cheese and bread. New World is run by the same co-operative as Pak'nSave and came out dearer than both — {threeNW} against Woolworths {threeW} and Pak'nSave {threeP} on the {threeN} items priced at all three. Woolworths was last read on {basketAsOf}. A row joins these comparisons when each chain's reading is within 30 days of that round, because a row keeps its last regular price in any week that item is on special or the weekly read fails — so some rows are older than others, and the NZ Lunchbox Price Index gives every row its own date.
faq_q21: Do the prices include sales or specials?
faq_a21: Both, and they are kept separate on purpose. The baseline cost of every menu uses regular Woolworths shelf prices, refreshed weekly - that is the honest 'any week of the year' figure. On top of that, each Monday the Woolworths and New World mailers are transcribed and what is on special is recorded. A special only changes a price when it can be matched to the exact product at the same pack size and is actually cheaper than the price already tracked - otherwise the regular price stands and no discount badge appears. That bar is deliberately high, and most advertised specials do not clear it: a flyer's 'was' price is that brand's own regular price, which is often above what we already track. So the toggle mostly works by ranking cheaper lunches higher rather than by finding large discounts, and the saving shown is only the part that can be stood behind. Regular prices are tracked separately at the NZ Lunchbox Price Index, which is how you can tell a real discount from a sticker.
faq_q22: Can I build a shopping list for two weeks at once?
faq_a22: The planner currently generates one week at a time. For a two-week shopping list, we recommend generating two separate plans and combining the shopping lists manually. Many parents find it useful to generate both weeks on Sunday, then buy the non-perishable items (canned goods, pasta, crackers, etc.) for both weeks at once, and pick up fresh items (bread, fruit, deli meats) at the start of each week. This approach reduces shopping trips while keeping ingredients fresh.
faq_q23: Does the planner check that meals are nutritionally balanced?
faq_a23: Honest answer: the planner does not check a week against the Ministry of Health's four food groups. There is no food-group logic in the code. What it does is enforce variety across recipe categories (Sandwich, Hot, Baking, Cold) so a week is not five sandwiches, apply your allergy and dietary filters, and show an estimated calorie figure per lunch based on standard portion sizes. That estimate is not a substitute for a nutrition plan. The nutrition writing on this site — the complete nutrition guide in particular — is benchmarked against Ministry of Health and Heart Foundation NZ guidance and cites its sources. If your child has specific dietary requirements, see a registered dietitian.
faq_q24: Are portion sizes appropriate for different age groups?
faq_a24: Our standard serve is sized for primary school children aged 5-12, which covers Years 1-8 in the NZ school system, and every cost elsewhere on this site — articles, the homepage and the price figures — is on that basis. In the planner you can change it under Portion size: Kindy (about ×{kindyFactor}), Primary Years 1–6 (×{primaryFactor}), Intermediate Years 7–8 (×{intermediateFactor}), College Years 9–13 (×{collegeFactor}) or Adult (×{adultFactor}). The planner multiplies each ingredient's share of a pack — and so the cost and the calorie figure — by that ratio; the menus stay the same. The ratios come from average daily energy needs by age in the Nutrient Reference Values for Australia and New Zealand (NHMRC / NZ Ministry of Health), so they are an estimate rather than a prescription, and single items like one egg or one yoghurt pot don't scale neatly. The calorie figure is a rough estimate rather than a target. Children still vary a lot: if they consistently bring food home, reduce the portion; if they're hungry after school, add an extra component like a piece of fruit or a small muesli bar. The Kindy (under 5) option under Allergies / Restrictions is separate: it leaves out foods with a high choking risk for young children, and ticking it also sets Portion size to Kindy.
faq_q25: How do you calculate the nutritional information?
faq_a25: Our calorie figure is a rough estimate. For each ingredient we take a generic energy value per 100g and a typical portion weight and add them up; an ingredient we have no value for gets a small flat allowance. These are generic values, not figures from a named food composition database or from the labels of the products we price, so treat the number as a ballpark — it is not precise enough for clinical use. We do not calculate protein, sugar or other nutrients. Actual values will vary with the brands and quantities you use. For children with medical conditions that require precise nutritional tracking (such as diabetes), please use a clinical-grade food tracking tool and consult your healthcare provider.
faq_q26: Can I share my plan with my partner or co-parent?
faq_a26: Yes. The easiest way is to download the plan as a PDF and share it via email, a messaging app, or AirDrop. The PDF has the 5-day menu — each lunch with its main ingredients, estimated cost and calories — and the full shopping list, which covers what your partner needs for the shop. It does not include the recipe steps; open a lunch on the planner screen to see how to make it. With a free account you can also send the PDF to your own email address using the 'Email Plan' button and forward it from there. We're considering adding shared accounts for families, where both parents can access and edit the same plan — let us know via the Contact page if this would be useful for your family.
faq_q27: How do I report a bug or incorrect recipe?
faq_a27: We appreciate your help in keeping Kiwi Lunchbox accurate! Head to our Contact page and select 'Technical Support' as the subject. Please include as much detail as possible: the recipe name, what seems incorrect (wrong ingredient, allergy tag error, broken pricing, etc.), and if it's a technical issue, your browser name and version plus a screenshot if possible. We review all reports and aim to fix confirmed issues within 48 hours for allergy-related errors, or within one week for other corrections. Your feedback directly improves the experience for all NZ families using the planner.
faq_q28: Is my data secure? What do you store?
faq_a28: We take data security seriously. If you create an account, we store your email address and the recipes you mark as favourites, using Supabase (a SOC 2-compliant database platform). Your meal plans are not stored on our servers — the last plan you generated is kept only in your own browser. We do not store payment information, dietary health records, or any information about your children. Cookies are used to remember your preferences (such as language) and your sign-in session. Google Analytics 4 collects anonymous usage statistics (pages visited, session duration, device type) with IP anonymisation enabled, and it only loads if you accept cookies in the cookie banner. Google AdSense uses cookies to serve ads; you can turn off personalised ads in Google's Ads Settings. We never sell your personal data. For full details, see our Privacy Policy.
faq_q29: Can I use the planner offline?
faq_a29: You need an internet connection to generate a plan, because plans are built on our server. Prices are not fetched live: they come from a weekly Woolworths price table that is bundled with the site when it is published. Once you've generated a plan, you can download it as a PDF, which works fully offline. One way to use it: generate the plan when you have Wi-Fi, save the PDF to your phone's Files app, and refer to it through the week without a connection.
faq_q30: How often is the recipe database updated?
faq_a30: Menus are added in small batches rather than on a fixed schedule. Each one is costed against tracked Woolworths prices, tagged for the six dietary filters (nut-free, dairy-free, gluten-free, egg-free, vegetarian, vegan) and checked against what is actually stocked in New Zealand supermarkets. Prices move faster than menus: every chain column in the price index is refreshed weekly from that chain's own online shop, and the current mailer specials are recorded every Monday. This is a one-person project, so there is no editorial team — just me and the receipts. Recipe suggestions are welcome via the Contact page.

planner_seo_title: Create Your Perfect Weekly School Lunch Plan
planner_seo_intro: Kiwi Lunchbox is a free school lunch planner for New Zealand families. It builds a five-day plan from a menu set tagged for nut-free, dairy-free, gluten-free, egg-free, vegetarian and vegan diets, and prices every day against Woolworths shelf prices tracked week by week. With the specials option on (the default), lunches are ranked by what they cost after this week's Woolworths and New World specials, so cheaper ones come up more often. Each plan comes with a shopping list and a costed total, so you know the number before you get to the checkout.
planner_seo_step1_text: Select any allergy filters (nut-free, dairy-free, gluten-free, egg-free, sesame-free) or dietary preferences (vegetarian, vegan). You can also exclude specific ingredients your child dislikes and add fridge leftovers you'd like to use up.
planner_seo_step2_text: Click 'Generate Plan' and the planner assembles a five-day menu in seconds, varied across categories rather than scored for nutritional balance. Each day shows a main, snacks, the full ingredient list, the method, and the estimated cost worked out as a portion of each pack.
planner_seo_step3_text: Download your plan as a PDF, email it to yourself, or share it. The shopping list is grouped by aisle with Woolworths price estimates — ready to take to the supermarket.
planner_seo_allergy_p: Every meal plan is built around your family's dietary filters. The database of {menuCount} New Zealand recipes is tagged for six filters — nut, dairy, gluten, egg, vegetarian and vegan — and a filtered plan only draws on recipes carrying that tag. A seventh filter, sesame, has no recipe tag: it is read from the allergen labels of the products behind each ingredient. The tag describes the recipe, not the packet: brands reformulate and shared production lines exist, so for a serious allergy the label on the product you buy is the thing that decides, not this filter. That is the same caution given on the FAQ and terms pages, and it is meant literally.
planner_seo_price_p: Prices come from Woolworths NZ's online catalogue and are refreshed once a week. Each ingredient shows its unit price and portion cost, so you can see what the week is actually worth rather than what you carry home. Pak'nSave is not priced inside the planner — for a store-by-store comparison see the NZ Lunchbox Price Index, which tracks 20 staples at Woolworths and Pak'nSave, adds New World where its price is fresh enough to compare, and says plainly when readings are too far apart in time to compare. Across our full menu set the median lunchbox is about $3.80 a day, or roughly $19 for five days.
planner_seo_howto_name: How to Create a Weekly School Lunch Plan
planner_seo_howto_desc: Use Kiwi Lunchbox to generate a personalised 5-day school lunch plan with allergy filters, shopping lists, and NZ supermarket prices.
home_guide_rules_p1: New Zealand schools take food safety seriously, and policies vary between schools. Many primary schools have a nut policy, and the words mean different things: 'nut-free' usually means no peanut butter, tree nuts or Nutella, while 'nut-aware' usually means nuts are discouraged but not banned. Before the school year starts, check your school's newsletter or office for their specific food policy.
home_guide_rules_p2: Many NZ schools also follow a 'water-only' or 'water and milk only' drink policy during school hours, so juice boxes, flavoured milk and fizzy drinks are often not allowed. Kiwi Lunchbox does not apply your school's policy for you: with no filters ticked, the menu includes peanut butter sandwiches and baked treats like brownies. Tick Nut Allergy (and any other filter your school or child needs) before you generate, and check the week against your school's rules.
home_guide_seasonal_h: Seasonal Meal Planning for NZ School Terms
home_guide_seasonal_p1: New Zealand's school year runs from early February to mid-December, split into four terms with two-week breaks between them. Because NZ is in the southern hemisphere, Term 1 starts in summer heat and Term 3 falls in the middle of winter — this significantly affects what you can pack safely.
home_guide_term1_desc: Summer/autumn — focus on cold lunches, fresh salads, rice paper rolls. Keep an ice pack in every lunchbox.
home_guide_term2_desc: Autumn into winter — perfect for thermos meals like soup, pasta, fried rice. Warm comfort food keeps energy up.
home_guide_term3_desc: Late winter/spring — transition meals. Wraps and scrolls work well as the weather slowly warms.
home_guide_term4_desc: Spring/summer — back to cold options. Sushi, sandwiches, and fruit-heavy boxes shine in the heat.
home_guide_nutrition_h: Nutrition Basics for NZ School Lunches
home_guide_nutrition_p1: New Zealand's Ministry of Health builds its eating guidelines around four food groups: vegetables and fruit; grain foods; milk and milk products; and legumes, nuts, seeds, fish and other seafood, eggs, poultry and red meat. A practical rule of thumb for a lunchbox — ours, not the Ministry's — is to pack from at least three of them: a protein such as chicken, egg, legumes or cheese, a grain food such as wholegrain bread, rice or pasta, and vegetables or fruit. A lunchbox covers morning tea and lunch together — around a third of a child's daily energy, based on New Zealand Child Nutrition Survey data.
home_guide_nutrition_p2: For portions, a rough rule of thumb is a protein serve about the size of your child's palm, carbs about the size of their fist, and vegetables filling at least a quarter of the box — a common guide, not an official NZ standard. Kiwi Lunchbox shows an estimated calorie figure for each day's lunchbox — that is the only nutrition number it calculates. It does not compute protein or other macronutrients, and none of the guidance above comes from the planner.
home_tips_heading: Get the Most from Kiwi Lunchbox
home_tips_prep_p: The most effective way to use Kiwi Lunchbox is to generate your plan on Sunday evening. Open the planner, set any dietary filters, and hit Generate. In about five seconds you'll have a complete Monday-to-Friday meal plan. Download the PDF shopping list, do your grocery run at Woolworths or Pak'nSave, and spend 30-45 minutes prepping components that store well: wash and chop vegetables, cook a batch of pasta or rice, boil eggs, and portion out cheese and crackers. On weekday mornings, assembly takes under five minutes per lunchbox because everything is ready to go.
home_tips_combo_p: The blog has {posts} in-depth posts covering budget recipes under $3 a meal, allergy-specific guides for nut-free, egg-free and multi-allergy families, and what regular shelf prices have actually done over the months I have been recording them. There are {guides} longer reference guides alongside them. After generating your plan, browse related posts for prep tips, batch cooking and seasonal NZ produce.
home_tips_allergy_h: Making the Most of Allergy Filters
home_tips_allergy_p: Kiwi Lunchbox supports seven allergy and dietary filters: nut-free, dairy-free, gluten-free, egg-free, sesame-free, vegetarian, and vegan. You can combine multiple filters — for example, selecting both 'nut-free' and 'dairy-free' leaves out every meal and snack flagged for either. The Exclude Ingredients list goes further: tap an ingredient your child won't eat, such as Capsicum, and any meal or snack that lists it is left out of generated plans. The match is on the exact name in the list, so check near neighbours too — Avocado and Tuna/Chicken/Avocado are separate entries. You can also type a fridge leftover into the input field, and the planner will try to work it into the weekly plan to reduce food waste.
home_tips_price_p: Every ingredient in your shopping list shows an estimated price sourced from Woolworths NZ. Prices marked 'Weekly' come from Woolworths' online catalogue and are refreshed once a week, so treat them as a recent shelf price rather than a live one; prices marked 'Est.' are estimates used when an item isn't in that week's pull. We also calculate a 'portion cost' — the actual amount of each ingredient you'll use per meal, not the full packet price. For example, a {cheesePack} block of cheese costs {cheesePackPrice} and covers about {cheeseServes} lunchboxes, so the portion cost shown next to cheese is {cheeseServe} — not {cheesePackPrice}. Across our full menu set the median lunchbox works out at about $3.80 a day, so a five-day week lands near $19 — cheaper if you pick from the lower end of the range.
planner_cost_basis: Estimated ingredient cost: every ingredient in the meal plus the snacks listed above, each costed as the share of a supermarket pack you'd actually use. It does not include a drink, or anything shown in the photo that isn't on the ingredient list. Photos are illustrative.
faq_q31: What exactly is included in the cost estimate?
faq_a31: Each day's figure covers every ingredient in the meal, plus the snacks listed on that card. Each ingredient is costed as the share of a supermarket pack you'd actually use — two slices from a loaf, not the whole loaf. It does not include a drink, or anything visible in a photo that isn't on the ingredient list; the photos are illustrative rather than a picture of the exact box. Prices come from Woolworths NZ and move week to week. In July 2026 we found and fixed a bug that had been mis-costing pack fractions, so figures published before then were unreliable — the numbers you see now are recalculated. Across our full menu set a box currently works out at a median of about {boxMedian}, ranging from roughly {boxFloor} to {boxCeiling} depending on the main.
faq_q32: Can I use these plans for my own lunch, not just the kids?
faq_a32: Yes. The menus are built around a school lunchbox, but none of them are only for children — they are ordinary meals in lunchbox form. If you are already making one, the simplest approach is a bigger portion of the same meal, drawn from the shopping list you already have. One thing to keep in mind: an adult portion will cost more than a child's. The planner's Portion size setting has an Adult option that scales each ingredient's share by about ×{adultFactor} — an estimate from average daily energy needs for adults compared with children aged 5–12, from the Nutrient Reference Values for Australia and New Zealand. The per-box costs elsewhere on the site are for a child's lunchbox. We would rather say that than let you plan a week's budget on a number that does not fit.
faq_q33: Can I use the planner for a kindy lunchbox?
faq_a33: Yes, with one setting. Tick Kindy (under 5) under Allergies / Restrictions before you generate a plan. The planner then leaves out the foods that the Ministry of Health's guidance on reducing food-related choking at early learning services says to exclude — for example dried fruit, popcorn, chips, hard rice crackers and sausages — and each day lists how to prepare the foods the guidance says to alter, such as grating raw apple or carrot, quartering grapes and cherry tomatoes, and chopping meat small. We also leave out roasted chickpeas; that one is our own call, not the guidance's. Ticking it also sets Portion size to Kindy, which scales the standard 5–12 serve to about ×{kindyFactor} — an estimate from average energy needs, which you can change. If your kindy has its own food rules, follow those. The kindy lunchbox guide in our Guides section goes through each rule.
